transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Amir (CTO - NexaHealth), Lena (ML Eng), Priya (Security)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, quick intro from our side, im sophie chen, account exec, and diego is our se who will do the tech mapping and demo.
[00:12] Amir: hey thanks, im amir, quick note - we're evaluating moving a lot of our conversational workflows off OpenAI into something we can control more, also have some Anthropic models in a few services and a together.ai contract for research. main drivers are latency, cost, and PHI concerns.
[00:26] Sophie: totally, that's exactly why we put together a parity walkthrough. goal: show how existing calls translate to Redwood API, what changes in streaming/function-calling, embeddings, and what to expect for latency/cost and deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private).
[00:40] Diego: quick agenda - mapping for chat APIs (messages vs prompts), function/tool calling, streaming tokens, embedding dims and normalization, batching/kv cache implications, then demo a live migration snippet and the console.

[01:05] Amir: do you have an example of function calls? We use a lot of structured tool calls in our triage flow.
[01:12] Diego: yeah so on OpenAI you have messages+functions+function_call, on Anthropic the API is slightly different (they call them instructions), and Together has its own wrapper. On Redwood we provide a drop-in mapping layer. Example: you still send messages with roles system/user/assistant, functions are defined as json schema, and Redwood will return a function_call in the assistant message. small differences: Redwood's function_call object includes a field "matched_model_variant" when we fallback to distilled variants, and the streaming chunk frames include an optional "tool_hint" segment for partial tool args.
[01:46] Lena: is that hint reliable for our telemetry? we parse partial JSON right now and it's flaky.
[01:52] Diego: noted, the hint is best-effort; for mission critical we recommend enabling full-function buffering by setting streaming_mode=buffered which will delay first bytes slightly but guarantee valid JSON in the last frame. we'll include the client snippet.

[02:20] [Speaker 1]: question on token accounting — how do max_tokens and stop sequences map?
[02:26] Sophie: good one. Redwood maps max_new_tokens to the same semantic as OpenAI's max_tokens in generation calls; for chat-style messages the token accounting includes prefix tokens for system messages, same as you'd expect. stop sequences are supported; note Redwood also offers per-route token caps and token-level cost breakdown per request in the console.

[02:50] Amir: embeddings — we currently use OpenAI embeddings (text-embedding-3-small) for similarity search. will those indexes be compatible?
[02:59] Diego: embeddings are vector outputs; Redwood supports the common dims (1536, 1024, 3072 depending on model) and we have an embeddings mapping guide. For migration we usually: 1) run embeddings side-by-side for a period, 2) compare cosine distances and reindex if the dimensionality differs. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization for storage and batch embedding jobs.
[03:25] Priya: encryption and audit logs — we have PHI, need KMS and long audit retention.
[03:32] Sophie: understood. Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated options both support customer-managed KMS and audit logs export. SOC 2 is in place; we can send the compliance pack. For on-prem or air-gapped we have a private package with HSM options. we'll share the security docs after the call.

[03:55] Diego: demo time - ive got a code snippet showing a direct replacement for an OpenAI chat call. (screen share)
[04:02] Diego: OpenAI call: openai.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-4o', messages: [...] , max_tokens: 400, temperature: 0.2 }) 
[04:12] Diego: Redwood equivalent: redwood.chat.create({ model: 'redwood/gpt4o-compatible', messages: [...], max_new_tokens: 400, temp: 0.2 }) — under the hood we map role->role, and for streaming you subscribe to a SSE endpoint that yields partial tokens with a slightly different envelope.
[04:32] Amir: any changes in rate limits or batching behavior we should expect? we typically do bursts up to ~120 rps for alerts.
[04:40] Diego: hosted tier has burst allowances; for steady burst patterns we recommend Redwood Dedicated where you reserve GPU capacity and get predictable throughput. Dedicated also gives you lower tail latency because you avoid multi-tenant queuing. For cost, batching and KV cache can reduce token cost by around 20-40% depending on prompt reuse.

[05:05] Lena: KV cache - we rely on cached conversation state to avoid re-sending long histories. how strict is the compatibility? last time an engine switched models our cache keys changed.
[05:14] Diego: good point. Redwood's KV cache is keyed by model_id + prompt_signature + user_id; if you pin model variants the keys stay stable. when switching model families you may need a short reindex window. We surface cache miss rates in the console so you can monitor.

[05:40] Sophie: talk about costs briefly - we can provide hosted usage vs committed dedicated pricing in the doc. also Optimize can run a quick profile and recommend quantization or batching config.

[05:55] [00:06:00] Diego: show console - per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, trace to requests, and a rollout panel (canary percentages, fallback). this is useful so that when you switch model variants (eg openai -> redwood/gpt4o-compatible) you can route 10% traffic and monitor evals.

[06:20] Amir: regulators ask for data residency - europe only, can you pin regions?
[06:26] Sophie: yes we have region pinning for hosted and Dedicated; Private can be fully on-prem. We'll include the region availability matrix.

[06:40] Priya: about PII/PHI - do logs contain prompts? can we redact?
[06:45] Diego: logs default to pseudonymized traces but you can enable prompt redaction at ingestion, and for private deployments you can disable logs entirely or route them to your SIEM via secure forwarding. KMS-managed envelope encryption is supported.

[07:05] [00:07:30] Amir: on latency numbers - what should we expect for 2048 token flows?
[07:10] Diego: on a dedicated GPU pool with optimized kernels we hit ~120-200 ms per token for certain model sizes; hosted varies but often is 150-300 ms depending on load. note that quantized models and batching change throughput/latency tradeoffs: int8 quantized models often reduce memory and improve throughput but slightly increase per-token latency on some hardware. we'll provide model perf profiles.

[07:40] Lena: is there a one-click migration for embeddings indexes?
[07:44] Sophie: not one-click; typical approach: run embeddings in parallel for a short window, compare vectors and reindex if dims change. our onboarding team can help with migration scripts.

[08:05] Diego: i'll show a Together.ai mapping - Together uses a 'prompt' wrapper and slightly different sampling params; Redwood maps top_p/temperature/n to equivalent fields. there's also logit_bias support and we expose lower-level controls if you need them.

[08:30] [Speaker 2]: any gotchas with compliance scanning tools?
[08:34] Priya: our DLP scans need full request payloads for audit but only allowed in our VPC.
[08:39] Diego: for that we recommend Private (on-prem) or Dedicated with private networking; we can set up secure forwarding for logs to your DLP.

[08:55] Sophie: ok lets go through a sample migration plan: 1) parallel run for 2 weeks with traffic split, 2) run automated evals on your prompt testset to verify quality parity, 3) run perf benchmarks with KiB-sized and 2k token sequences, 4) make decision to cutover or continue dedicated.

[09:20] Amir: rough timeline - we want a pilot by mid-december if possible.
[09:24] Sophie: reasonable. we'll start by sending a migration checklist and parity mapping doc today.

[09:35] Diego: demo wrap - i've dropped a sample migration gist into the chat with code for streaming and for buffered function calls (link: https://redwood.example/migration/gists/stream-to-buffer).

[09:50] Lena: does the SDK support both openai-compatible args and native ones? we want minimal code changes.
[09:55] Diego: yep, our SDK has a compatibility shim so you can call redwood.openaiCompat.chatCreate(...) which accepts OpenAI-style args then forwards to the native endpoint; it's helpful for quick lifts. We'll share the doc.

[10:15] Priya: last question - vulnerability disclosure and pen tests?
[10:18] Sophie: we run quarterly pen tests and can share an executive summary and the redacted report. we'll include SOC 2 attest and our pen test cadence in the security pack.

[10:35] Amir: thanks this was helpful. next steps summarized?
[10:40] Sophie: action items - sarah will send the docs (note: typo, sarah-> i mean sophie), diego will prepare benchmark script, amir will share sample prompts. schedule se deep-dive for networking early next week.

Action Items (as said in call):
- Sophie Chen: Send parity mapping doc, pricing for hosted/dedicated, and security pack (SOC 2 & pen test summary) — due 2026-12-05
- Diego Martinez: Provide benchmark script + instructions for latency traces, and a small dataset for embedding side-by-side test — due 2026-12-04
- Amir Patel: Share sanitized sample prompts and QPS profile — due 2026-12-03

Links shared during call:
- Migration deck (redwood): https://redwood.example/decks/migration-parity.pdf

End of transcript.
